parent-material.def: The rock or sediment a soil forms from: the bedrock under it, or material carried in by rivers, glaciers or wind. It sets which minerals the soil starts with.

humus.def: Dark, crumbly organic matter in soil, left when decomposers break down dead plants and animals. It holds water and slowly releases nutrients.

soil-horizon.def: One of the layers in a soil profile: O (organic matter), A (topsoil, humus mixed with minerals), B (subsoil, where leached minerals collect), C (partly weathered parent material), then bedrock.

erosion.def: The removal and transport of soil or rock by wind, water or ice. It speeds up where plants are removed and the ground is left bare.
